item.title: Gradient AI launches underwriting tool
item.description: Gradient AI has launched Sentinel, a group health underwriting tool that uses lab results to identify potentially high-cost conditions before they appear in medical or pharmacy claims. The tool uses the same census information as SAIL, allowing existing customers to add it to their underwriting workflow without adopting a separate system. Sentinel is available as an add-on to SAIL, the company’s group health and stop-loss underwriting platform.

item.title: Amwins launches clinical trials insurance product
item.description: Amwins has launched an exclusive clinical trials insurance product through its Brokerage division, offering $25 million limits on paper pre-licensed in more than 115 countries. The product was developed with an unnamed Lloyd’s syndicate and is available exclusively through Amwins brokers. Coverage includes clinical trials indemnity, no-fault compensation, clinical testing liability, public and products liability, professional liability and medical malpractice.

For Karan Mishra, the opportunity for AI in insurance begins with familiar operational problems: gathering documents, checking requirements and moving information between organizations and systems. “Well, the metaphor is you’re stitching gaps within systems,” says Mishra, CEO, StitchStudio. item.title: NYT Must Face Trump $15 Billion Defamation Suit, Judge Rules
item.description: Related: WSJ Wins Dismissal of Trump’s $10 Billion Defamation Suit The judge ruled that Trump plausibly alleged that the journalists made decisive allegations of complex crimes without obtaining the kind of explicit expert opinion Merryday said was necessary to support them. A federal judge allowed President Donald Trump to proceed with portions of his $15 billion defamation lawsuit against the New York Times and Penguin Random House LLC, giving a boost to his ongoing cases against the press. District Judge Steven Merryday in Tampa, Florida, on Thursday denied a request by one of the world’s most prominent news organizations and the publisher to fully dismiss the case.

item.title: Allianz Commercial warns AI-related insurance claims could mask greater financial exposure
item.description: Allianz Commercial, the corporate insurance business of global insurer Allianz Group, has warned that the financial impact of artificial intelligence (AI) on businesses could be considerably greater than current insurance claims suggest, with the increasing use of the technology creating new sources of legal, operational and financial risk. According to Allianz Commercial, these cases demonstrate how AI-related disputes can develop into substantial insurance exposures, particularly when litigation involves several parties or raises wider questions about corporate accountability. Nevertheless, Allianz Commercial notes that AI would not currently feature among the 20 largest sources of commercial insurance losses based on confirmed claims data.

item.title: Ansay & Associates Acquires Wisconsin’s Meyer Insurance
item.description: Ansay & Associates has acquired Wisconsin’s Meyer Agency, a third-generation family-owned agency based in Sauk Prairie, Wisconsin. Going forward, the agency will operate as “Meyer Insurance, a division of Ansay & Associates,” reflecting the integration of the two organizations. Founded in 1919 by Rolf Meyer, Meyer Insurance has been involved in the Sauk Prairie community for more than a century.

item.title: People Moves: Brown & Riding Adds Vu to Management & Professional Liability Practice
item.description: Brown & Riding has added Anna Vu to its national management & professional liability practice. “We are happy to welcome Anna to Brown & Riding,” said Jeff Rodriguez, President and Chief Executive Officer. Her deep expertise, genuine care for the people she works with, and relentless focus on finding the right solutions reflect the characteristics we value at B&R.” Vu has more than 20 years of experience and specializes in directors & officers, employment practices liability, fiduciary liability, crime, cyber liability, healthcare, and errors & omissions coverage.

item.title: North Dakota Drillers Tap Trucks as Pipe Outage Disrupts Flows
item.description: North Dakota oil producers are moving Bakken crude oil by truck as a prolonged outage of an Enbridge Inc.-operated pipeline forces drillers to look for alternatives to avoid shutting in production. The North Dakota Pipeline has been operating at lower rates since last week after a surge in reports of tainted crude forced operator Enbridge to implement testing for organic chlorides, slowing down the system. Read more: Marathon Issues Force Majeure for North Dakota Oil Deliveries The North Dakota Pipeline hauls Bakken oil to refiners in the US and Canada.

item.title: Oliver Wyman to acquire Synpulse
item.description: Oliver Wyman , Marsh’s management consulting business, has agreed to acquire Synpulse , a technology consultancy that serves insurers, banks and wealth managers. The acquisition adds Synpulse’s AI engineering and systems modernization capabilities, giving Oliver Wyman more capacity to help insurers and other financial institutions replace legacy systems and put new technology into production. Founded in 1996, Synpulse has about 1,200 employees across more than 20 locations.

item.title: ADP acquires ZenBusiness
item.description: ADP has acquired ZenBusiness , an Austin-based platform that helps entrepreneurs form businesses and stay compliant. Founded in 2015, ZenBusiness has helped more than one million entrepreneurs start a business, according to ADP. ZenBusiness once listed Bold Penguin as a partner and now includes a business insurance quote from ERGO Next Insurance in its Pro formation package.

item.description: AI experimentation is everywhere in insurance, but turning experiments into results is rare. Bolt agency has been using AI in its day-to-day operations for the past 18 months. Bound policies are up 41%, and call abandonment has dropped about 20%.

item.title: Commercial Property Premium Decreases of 6.2% Drive Overall Soft Q3: CIAB
item.description: Survey-takers reported decreases in premiums for nine lines of business: business interruption, construction, commercial property, cyber, directors and officers, employment practices, surety bonds, terrorism, and workers compensation. Soft market conditions remain stubborn, with no “meaningful” change for average commercial insurance premiums in third-quarter 2026 compared with the prior quarter. The Council of Insurance Agents & Brokers (CIAB)’s latest market survey found premium decreased an average of 1.3% for Q3 across all account sizes.

item.description: The defunding of weather observation systems across the world as countries focus on military spending is making it harder to predict extreme events at a time when the planet is reaching unprecedented heat levels. Weather and climate observations worth about $10 billion globally are at risk, according to the World Meteorological Organization . In terms of observations, she added, “We are increasingly far from solving a problem that’s not hard to solve.” Data gathered in hundreds of weather stations across the world are essential to allow forecasters to make predictions on storms, heat waves and drought.

item.title: What The Telecom Bust Taught Me About AI’s Debt Boom
item.description: The financing of the AI buildout is shifting from equity to debt, and those who invested through the telecom bubble may recognize what that shift tends to mean. By 2002 the telecom sector carried roughly $1 trillion in debt , much of which the chairman of the FCC told Congress would never be repaid, and WorldCom had entered what was then the largest bankruptcy in American history . Over the past year, more of the stack has started running on debt rather than equity, and in my experience, that crossing is the moment the telecom bubble becomes the relevant history given that debt may change how these stories end.

item.title: 5 Interesting Startup Deals You May Have Missed: Reflecting Sunlight From Space, Better Breathing And Smarter Garbage Trucks
item.description: This is a monthly column that runs down five interesting startup funding deals that may have flown under the radar. Our latest roundup also includes a company bringing AI to the old-school business of garbage hauling, another rethinking how factories are programmed, and a consumer brand betting that better breathing could become a big business. The Hawthorne, California-based startup wants to put giant mirrors in orbit to redirect sunlight toward specific locations on Earth, potentially allowing solar farms to keep generating electricity longer after sunset.

item.title: Liberty Mutual targets $300m multi-peril reinsurance with twelfth Mystic Re cat bond
item.description: Liberty Mutual Insurance has returned to the catastrophe bond market with an initial target to secure $300 million of indemnity based, multi-peril catastrophe reinsurance protection from the capital markets through a Mystic Re IV Ltd. Two tranches of Series 2027-1 notes are being offered to cat bond investors, with the issuance designed to provide Liberty Mutual at least $300 million in multi-peril, multi-year collateralized reinsurance protection. The Mystic Re IV 2027-1 cat bond notes will provide Liberty Mutual with reinsurance protection against losses from named storms, earthquakes, severe weather and wildfires on an indemnity trigger and per-occurrence basis, with the covered area being the US, Canada and the Caribbean.

item.title: AM Best expects more measured growth in delegated underwriting market
item.description: AM Best, the credit rating agency, has retained its stable outlook for the delegated underwriting authority enterprise (DUAE) market, as expectations of slower premium growth coincide with greater scrutiny of underwriting practices and a more selective approach to capacity allocation. “Stricter governance and audit requirements are becoming standard, as carriers intensify their reviews of underwriting authority, claims handling and data integrity.” According to AM Best, competitive pressures are becoming more pronounced as the delegated underwriting market develops. In its report, Market Segment Outlook: Delegated Underwriting Authority Enterprises , AM Best describes the sector as an established component of the insurance market, providing specialist underwriting capabilities to capacity providers across different classes of business, industries and international territories.

item.description: Florida Insurance and Reinsurance (Florida Re), a Tampa-domiciled, dual-licensed insurer and reinsurer backed by MNK Group, has appointed Chris Griffith as Chief Executive Officer following approval by the Florida Office of Insurance Regulation. “Drawing on extensive experience across Florida and the broader US market, Chris brings valuable insight into evolving risks and opportunities, enabling us to continue developing tailored solutions for our clients.” Griffith added, “I am delighted to be leading Florida Re as we enter the next phase of our development. Griffith has deep expertise across the US insurance industry, particularly in the Florida and coastal property markets.

item.title: Ransomware incidents rise 38% in Q3’26 as attackers exploit vulnerabilities: Beazley Security
item.description: Reported ransomware incidents increased 38% in the third quarter of 2026 compared with the previous quarter, according to Beazley Security’s Q3 2026 Quarterly Threat Report. “Start with known exploited vulnerabilities and internet-facing applications, then prioritise systems that provide access to credentials, cloud infrastructure or critical business operations.” Despite rising patch volumes from major technology companies such as Microsoft and Oracle, the report found that many ransomware incidents that began with exploitation involved self-hosted, internet-facing applications such as build servers, analytics platforms and collaboration tools. In Q3 2026, threat actors exploited vulnerabilities in 28% of ransomware cases, double the 14% recorded in Q2.

item.title: FM to Send Workers to Massachusetts as Part of Headquarters Relocation
item.description: The global insurance company, formerly known as FM Global, is also sending an unspecified number of local workers to Massachusetts as part of a regional approach that includes facilities in Norwood and Boston, the company confirmed in a statement to Rhode Island Current Friday afternoon. Ahead of Johnston exodus, Polisena says FM to lay off local workers The confirmation comes four days after the commercial property insurer revealed that it plans to move out of its wooded campus off Central Avenue in Johnston by the end of 2027, relocating its global headquarters to downtown Providence. There will also be a “limited number” of workers laid off in conjunction with the move, the company said.

item.title: Alibaba Defrauded Investors by Over Ties to Alleged Spy in Nvidia Scandal: Lawsuit
item.description: Alibaba was sued on Thursday in New York by shareholders who accused the Chinese e-commerce giant of defrauding them by concealing its ties to the suspected Chinese spy whose relationship with former Nvidia Chief Executive Jensen Huang contributed to his resignation last week. The shareholders said Alibaba shares fell 14% over four days last week because of media reports on Alibaba’s ties to Alice Huang and Megaspeed, including that Alibaba had become Megaspeed’s “dominant” customer. Nvidia itself faces several shareholder lawsuits over the spy scandal, including allegations of lax oversight by its directors.

item.title: AI-related cyber risks drive growing insurance interest among UK SMEs, says Brit
item.description: According to Brit, these developments are having a direct bearing on demand for insurance, with more than two-thirds of SMEs reporting that AI-related risks have strengthened their interest in obtaining cyber protection. Concerns surrounding artificial intelligence and the increasing complexity of cyber attacks are influencing insurance decisions among UK small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), according to research published by Brit Insurance, a specialty insurance and reinsurance provider operating in the Lloyd’s market. The insurer’s findings indicate that 68% of SMEs are now more inclined to purchase cyber insurance because of risks associated with AI.

item.title: Kalshi Loses Bid to Prevent Maryland From Policing Prediction Market
item.description: A US appeals court on Tuesday ruled that Kalshi cannot prevent Maryland gaming regulators from pursuing enforcement actions against the prediction market operator for allowing users to place financial bets on sports without a license. Kalshi in a statement said Tuesday’s decision “demonstrates there is no unified coherent legal argument against prediction markets.” New Jersey Takes Fight Over Kalshi’s Prediction Market to US Supreme Court Jeremy Baker, the acting director of the Maryland Lottery and Gaming Control Commission, in a statement welcomed the ruling, saying it “affirmed the state’s ability to regulate what is clearly sports wagering.” Kalshi and similar companies allow users to trade on the outcomes of events such as sports and elections. The 2-1 decision by the Richmond, Virginia-based 4th US Circuit Court of Appeals deepens a split among federal appeals courts over whether state gaming regulators have the power to police prediction markets operated by Kalshi and competing platforms.
